title: VPC Peering and Shared VPC: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: You have two separate networks. They need to talk privately. There are two ways to do it.

scenes.heading: Apartments and a shared driveway
scenes.narration: Peering and sharing solve different problems. Peering joins two V P Cs directly and privately. It isn't transitive, so A to B and B to C doesn't give A to C. Shared V P C puts network control in one host project. Other projects, the service projects, use it.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. Peering isn't transitive. It's within one organisation. Peering is direct.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva peering and Shared VPC lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Peering is direct but not transitive. Shared V P C centralises control. Service projects use the host's network. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva peering and Shared VPC lab.
